claims: Journey mapping represents an end-to-end experience from the user's perspective so a team can see connected steps, boundaries, breakdowns, and opportunities.
A journey map should start from research about the steps users actually take and the transactions involved.
An experience map should make struggle points and candidate improvement areas visible.
A map can reveal dead ends where the user cannot continue toward the larger goal.
Journey analysis should include gaps between online and offline parts of a service.

anchors.quote: It's important for teams to make sure the thing they're building forms a coherent part of a user's wider journey.
Start by talking to your users to learn more about the steps they have to take and the transactions involved.
The map should show which bits of the journey users are struggling with and the areas you might want to focus on improving.
dead ends in the user journey
online and offline elements of the transaction not joining up in an intuitive way
